definitions.gloss: bulleted list; itemized list; listing by items
definitions.explanation: A way of writing that presents information as a series of separate points or items, each on its own line. Common in business documents, presentations, and instructions.

examples.japanese: {要点|ようてん}を{箇条書|かじょうが}きにする。
examples.english: To list the key points in bullet form.

examples.japanese: {報告書|ほうこくしょ}は{箇条書|かじょうが}きで{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: Please write the report in bulleted form.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{文章|ぶんしょう}より{箇条書|かじょうが}きのほうが{読|よ}みやすいので、{資料|しりょう}を{作|つく}り{直|なお}した。
examples.english: A bulleted list is easier to read than a long paragraph, so I redid the materials.

notes:
{箇条書|かじょうが}き refers to the format of writing information as a list of separate items or bullet points, rather than in paragraph form.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {箇条書|かじょうが}きにする: to put into list form
- {箇条書|かじょうが}きで{書|か}く: to write in list form
- {箇条書|かじょうが}きにまとめる: to organize into bullet points
- {箇条書|かじょうが}きで{示|しめ}す: to present in list form

WORD FORMATION:
{箇条|かじょう} (item, article) + {書|が}き (writing)

USAGE:
Very common in business documents, presentations, meeting minutes, and instructions. Often contrasted with {文章|ぶんしょう} (prose/paragraph form).

RELATED:
- {箇条|かじょう}: article, item
- {項目|こうもく}: item, heading
- {一覧|いちらん}: list, overview
